CHARLOTTE AND MECKLENBURG COUNTY FIRST RESPONDERS ARRIVED AND SECURED THE AREA. BOTH INJURED PARTIES WERE TRANSPORTED TO A LOCAL HOSPITAL FOR TREATMENT.

AT 0845 HOURS ON 02OCT2011, AT RICE YARD, WAYCROSS, GA, MILEPOST AN 587, A YARD EMPLOYEE SMELLED AN ODOR OF AMMONIA WHILE COUPLING RAILCARS ON TRACK B-62, CSX GENERAL CAR FOREMAN FOUND GLNX 34589 A LOAD, ANHYDROUS AMMONIA, UN1005, (NH3) CLASS 2.2, TO BE EMITTING THE ODOR, GLNX 34587 WAS ISOLATED AND A CSX EMERGENCY RESPONSE CONTRACTOR WAS CALLED TO INVESTIGATE, HANDLE AND SECURE THE TANK CAR. THE ER CONTRACTOR INVESTIGATED AND FOUND THE SECUREMENT SEALS INTACT, BUT THE A-END LIQUID LINE VALVE WAS OPEN 1/8 OF A TURN AND THE SECONDARY SECUREMENT PLUG WAS LESS THAN TOOL TIGHT, THE VALVE WAS CLOSED, THE PLUG WAS TIGHTENED AND THE RELEASE WAS SECURED.

SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 47.674444, -122.475556 (Explicit)
Report DescriptionTHIS IS A POTENTIAL RELEASE... INFORMATION RECEIVED FROM THE NATIONAL COMMAND CENTER AND USCG SECTOR PUGET SOUND... AT APPROXIMATELY 2000Z (1400 PST), WASHINGTON STATE FERRY WENATCHEE EXPERIENCED A FIRE IN THE NUMBER TWO ENGINE ROOM AFTER A CRANK CASE EXPLOSION WHILE CONDUCTING POWER TRIALS IN PUGET SOUND. THERE WERE NO PASSENGERS ON BOARD, ONLY 13 CREWMEMBERS. FERRY WENATCHEE WAS TOWED BY TUG TO EAGLE HARBOR IN BAINBRIDGE ISLAND. THE CREW AND LOCAL FIRE DEPARTMENT SUCCESSFULLY EXTINGUISHED FIRE. THE DAMAGE TO THE FERRY WENATCHEE IS VALUED TO BE IN EXCESS OF $500,000. THERE WERE NO INJURIES OR POLLUTION REPORTED. COAST GUARD RESPONDED WITH THREE SMALL BOATS, AND ONE COAST GUARD HELICOPTER. SECTOR PUGET SOUND INVESTIGATOR AND INSPECTOR RESPONDING. NO MEDIA ATTENTION AT THIS TIME. USCG CONFIRMED THERE WAS NO MATERIAL RELEASED FROM THIS INCIDENT. USCG STATED THERE WAS A POTENTIAL RELEASE OF AN UNKNOWN OIL AND DIESEL FUEL FROM THIS INCIDENT.

Report DescriptionCALLER REPORTED THAT THE SRP WAS PERFORMING A DEMOLITION OF THE CONTROL ENCLOSURE SUB-STATION WHICH HAD PREVIOUSLY IDENTIFIED LEAD BASED PAINT. PER THE ADVICE OF THE WASTE TEAM, THIS MATERIAL WAS SUPPOSED TO BE SEGREGATED AND HANDLED SEPARATELY BY DISPOSING IT TO SEPARATE A WASTE MANAGEMENT FACILITY FOR LEAD BASED PAINT. INSTEAD THE MATERIAL WENT TO HAMPTON ROADS RECOVERY CENTER IN CHESAPEAKE WITH OTHER NORMAL CONSTRUCTION DEBRIS. THEY ARE ESTIMATING LESS THAN 1 CUBIC YARD OF CONCRETE AND LEAD BASED PAINT WAS MIXED, AND THAT THE MATERIAL IS ABOVE THE REPORTABLE QUANTITY. DEMOLITION OCCURRED ON 7/9 OR 7/10 AND INCIDENT WAS REPORTED TO THE REPORTING PARTY ON 7/12 AFTER DISCOVERY BY THE SRP OF THE ERROR.
